messages:
maya: FYI, received a model drop for paperbark-8b from an external repo. Asking to triage for onboarding (hosted + dedicated) — need license check, export-control, and whether we can quantize/redistribute weights. Can someone take? :eyes:

carlos: link? I can do a quick license read and flag any redlines.

maya: repo: https://git.example.com/paperbark/paperbark-8b (license file at /LICENSE). brief: training logs claim mixed web/cc data, weights provided under a repo release. No explicit model card aside from README.

priya: skimmed LICENSE earlier — looks like "CC-BY-NC-4.0" with a contributor addendum that forbids commercial hosting unless you get a separate sublicense. also a clause about "no rehosting for profit" — need legal to confirm exact scope.

sam: tagging in. If it's CC-BY-NC, that forbids commercial use of the model. Hosting a paid API (hosted) definitely blocked. Dedicated/reserved capacity for a paying customer likely blocked too unless the customer is non-commercial. Private on-prem deployments for a paying customer are still commercial? depends on contract language — probably also restricted.

zane: quick operational Q: what about quantization? If we quantize the checkpoint and ship a quantized weight as part of a redistributable artifact, that might count as a derivative — same licensing implications. If we only do quantization inside a private customer environment (no redistribution), might be okay.

sam: correct. Quantized weights distributed to customers = redistribution of a derivative. We should treat distribution as subject to license. Running quantization in-house and serving via a hosted API is redistribution under many license interpretations, since the model is being used to provide a commercial service.

priya: proposed immediate actions: 1) confirm exact LICENSE text from the release (curl snippet below), 2) ask upstream for model card/provenance and contributor CLAs, 3) run an internal intake form to capture intended deployment modes, 4) Zane to run quant smoke tests in isolated env (no artifacts left), 5) legal to advise on non-commercial carveouts.

priya: `curl -sL https://git.example.com/paperbark/paperbark-8b/raw/main/LICENSE | sed -n '1,120p'`

zane: I'll spin a throwaway VM and run quantize + perf baseline with 4-bit recipes, will not persist weights. Will post perf numbers and whether accuracy drops >2% on our eval set.

maya: priority: medium. Product asked for feasibility for a pilot in private-dedicated only if licensing ok.

sam: legal next steps: 1) we need to confirm whether the repo's "contributor addendum" adds additional host restrictions; 2) confirm if the model weights were trained on licensed-protected datasets with additional covenants; 3) clarify whether the author will grant a commercial sublicense for enterprise customers (if they want hosted/dedicated). I can open a formal intake ticket.

carlos: also flag export control: training data has multilingual scraping, but authors are based in EU. We should run the standard export-control checklist. If any dual-use or restricted dataset flags, escalate.

legal-bot: Incidentally, our model-gate intake template is at https://redwood.internal/models/intake. Required fields: provenance, license scan, model card, export-control, training-data-PII-check, whitelabel-sublicense.

maya: thanks. Action items: Sam — open intake ticket & request upstream sublicense wording. Zane — quant smoke in isolated env. Carlos — license scan and export-control checklist. Priya — contact upstream for model card & contributor CLAs. I'll update roadmap. :thumbsup:
